title: Gemini Decisions API Launch: What Google Released
summary: Gemini Decisions API launch gives automations a faster way to handle routing and classification. Evaluate whether it fits your automation needs.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Four questions keep coming up, and the answers below come only from what Google has published, so several read "not published". Each gap is a thing to test yourself, not a thing to assume.


Google lists $0 for output tokens, with input at $0.10 per 1M tokens, and a no-cost tier in Google AI Studio for prototyping. Don't budget around a guess. Check Google's pricing page for the exact rate before you route real volume through it.


Do I need a developer to use the Gemini Decisions API? Google's page doesn't say. It is an API, so expect to send a request and read a response.


If you've wired a webhook into a spreadsheet before, you're likely close. Whether it needs more than that is not published.


Can I call it from a no-code workflow? A native connector for any automation tool is not published. The generic route is an HTTP request step in whatever builder you use.


That's the thing to try first in a single workflow, on a throwaway trigger, before you rely on it.


How is it different from calling a Gemini model directly? Google describes Gemini Decision as a model for fast yes/no and score decisions. A general Gemini model answers in open text, so the practical difference is a narrower job.


Limits, output format and availability are not published.


Those gaps are why the next step is a small comparison on your own tasks.
